title: The Euclidean coefficient norm is a continuous seminorm dominated by the operator norm, with nonexpansive radial retraction
statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ there is a constant c > 0 such that, writing |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α for α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n and ‖α‖ for the operator norm: (i) α ↦ |α|_E is continuous; (ii) |α + β|_E ≤ |α|_E + |β|_E for all α, β; (iii) |t•α|_E = |t|·|α|_E for all t ∈ ℝ and α; (iv) |α|_E ≤ c·‖α‖ for all α; (v) for all v, b with |b|_E ≤ 1, |(max 1 |v|_E)⁻¹ • v − b|_E ≤ |v − b|_E.
lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ Continuous (fun α : Covector (Euclid P) n => covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ α β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm (α + β) ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α + covectorEuclideanNorm β) ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), covectorEuclideanNorm (t • α) = |t| * covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ c * ‖α‖) ∧ ∀ v b : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm b ≤ 1 → covectorEuclideanNorm ((max 1 (covectorEuclideanNorm v))⁻¹ • v - b) ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm (v - b)
